title: I build my Android strategy game with Claude Code. This week a Claude session played a fresh install on my phone and found where new players quit
author: RoyFactory
selftext:
I'm a solo developer from Korea. Pixel Warlords: Three Kingdoms is a free Android strategy game (ads, optional ad removal): you recruit and upgrade troops in a camp, pick a formation on a 3x3 grid, and the battle plays out on its own. Early fights are about a hundred soldiers; by the last of the 24 chapters one battle has around 3,000 on the field.



Almost all of the code is written with Claude Code. Today's update (1.3.1) came out of an experiment I'd recommend: I had a Claude session play a fresh install on my phone like a new player. It drove the phone over adb with taps and screenshots, from the first launch to the end of chapter 1 (34 minutes) in Korean and through the first stages in Indonesian, and wrote down every place where it would have quit, ranked, with a screenshot for each. It was not allowed to change code during the run. Deciding what to fix was a separate step, and the fixes were checked by a separate QA session, which is a rule I keep everywhere: the session that makes a change never judges it.



The worst finding was one I would never have seen myself, because I know the game too well. After the first defeat, following the result screen's own Research button could leave you with 1 food and 55 soldiers. Every recruit button then said "not enough food" and tapping it did nothing. Buying food with gems was possible, but only by tapping the food counter at the top, which doesn't look like a button, and income alone would have taken over 50 minutes to rebuild the army. In 1.3.1 that button opens the same "buy the shortfall" window that upgrades and research already had, and you keep recruiting right there. The same run gave the smaller fixes too: the goal panel now shows the time left, new games start at 3x battle speed, and the formation goal now points to the Research tab, where you actually unlock formations.



The art started in PixelLab. For 1.3.0 I rebuilt almost all of it locally: a rig cuts each original idle sprite into parts and animates walk, attack and death from templates, and effects, icons and map props come from scripts. The bug that cost me the most was the pipeline reading the game folder as its source after the local versions had been installed there, so it was judging against its own output. The fix was a frozen copy of the originals that nothing is allowed to overwrite.



I'm curious whether others here use an agent as a first-time player, and how you keep it from playing like someone who already knows the game. Mine sends taps without reading, so its times are only a lower bound.



Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.royfactory.threekingdomstactics&referrer=utm\_source%3Dreddit\_aigamedev%26utm\_medium%3Dcommunity%26utm\_campaign%3Dv131vc30](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.royfactory.threekingdomstactics&referrer=utm_source%3Dreddit_aigamedev%26utm_medium%3Dcommunity%26utm_campaign%3Dv131vc30)

comments.author: No-Pollution7797
comments.body:
A lot of the knowing-too-much comes from what the session can see besides the screen. I'd run the player from an empty folder with no repo and no notes, so screenshots are all it has, and tell it nothing about the game beyond what the store page says.



For the tapping without reading, I'd have it write one line before every tap on what it expects that button to do, and one line after on what happened. The mismatches are the list I'd care about, since that's where a real newcomer gets confused, and it drags the run closer to reading speed. It still won't get bored the way a person does, so I'd read its quit points as places people get stuck and keep watching one real player for where they just lose interest.

replies.author: RoyFactory
replies.body:
That's a really good point. I run had the whole repo open, so when it flagged that the formation goal pointed to the wrong tab, part of that came from reading the code, not the screen

  
I'm going to redo it from an empty folder with only screenshots and the store description, and log an except, result line around every tap.  
  
I'll compare the mismatch list against this first run on the same version.



And agreed on boredom: my analytics funnel showed drop-offs in the same two places this run flagged, but it can't tell me why people stop.

  
Thanks for taking the time to write this.

replies.author: No-Pollution7797
replies.body: Same version is the right call. I'm curious whether the wrong tab one still shows up when all it has is the screen.

comments.author: IndiBestEngineer
comments.body:
"the session that makes a change never judges it" is the rule that stuck for me too. i run a bot that plays WoW the same way: a fix only counts once the old symptom had enough chances to come back and didn't. with too few chances it stays "not verified", so far that is 21 of 110 tickets, against 4 proven fixed.

did the QA session replay the fresh install from the start, or only check the screens that changed?

replies.author: RoyFactory
replies.body:
Both, partly. QA did a fresh install and played the first 10M from launch. Deeper states, like the stage 13 defeat with 1 food, it set up from a save file.

The replay is what paid off. Each changed screen worked alone, but together they pushed new players into a formation that lost 16 of 16 seeds at stage 2. On the phone, all 160 soldiers wiped at minute 4. Screen checks would have passed it.

By your standard my main fix is still "not verified", the symptom showed up once, and the fix was checked against a save. Live players are the real test, so I'll compare the funnel two weeks after the update.

Thanks, this was a useful push.

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: when you compare the funnel after this patch, i'd split players by device and by where they came from. a better result could come from a different group of players rather than the new tutorial. the same source and same kind of phone before and after the update would give you a cleaner signal.
